# Code of conduct

This is a small project about making software run. The rules are short because
the situations are few.

## What is expected

- Be plain and be accurate. Say what you observed, and say when you are
  guessing. A wrong answer stated confidently costs someone else an evening.
- Assume the other person is doing something reasonable for reasons you cannot
  see. Different distribution, different GPU, different Store build.
- Criticise the work, not the person. "This breaks on a fresh prefix" is fine
  at any volume. "You clearly did not test this" is not.
- Accept that maintainers are volunteers and that the answer may be no, or
  nothing at all. An unanswered issue is not an insult.

## What is not acceptable

- Harassment, personal attacks, or demeaning comments about anyone — including
  about people who are not here.
- Sexualised language or imagery, and unwelcome attention of any kind.
- Publishing anyone's private information: real name, address, email, employer,
  or account identifiers. **This includes another person's gamertag, XUID or
  PFID scraped from a log they posted.** If you spot one in someone else's
  report, say so privately rather than quoting it back at them in the thread.
- Sustained disruption: reopening a settled argument, demanding attention,
  filing the same issue repeatedly.

## Specific to this project

These are the ones that actually come up:

- **Do not ask anyone to share game content, a licence, a content key, a
  package, or account access.** Not in an issue, not in a review, not in a DM
  to a contributor. This project only ever works with games you own on your own
  account, and requests to change that are not a grey area.
- **Do not post credentials, yours or anyone else's.** If a token appears in a
  thread, do not quote it; report it (see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)) so it can
  be dealt with, and expect the comment to be removed rather than edited.
- **Do not use this project's issues to coordinate piracy**, or to ask how to
  defeat a title's own protection. The answer is no, and the thread will be
  locked.

## Scope

This applies in the repository — issues, pull requests, reviews, commit
messages, discussions — and to anywhere someone is representing the project.

## Reporting

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on this repository
(**Security → Advisories → Report a vulnerability**). It is private to the
maintainers and is the only private channel this repository has; it is fine to
use it for conduct reports as well as security ones. Include links to the
comments and say what you want to happen.

If the report is about a maintainer, or you would rather it did not reach them,
use [GitHub's own abuse reporting](https://github.com/contact/report-abuse).

## Enforcement

A maintainer will read it and respond. Depending on what happened, that means:
a private word, a comment removed, an issue locked, or a block. Content that
carries someone's credentials or private data is removed rather than edited,
because an edited comment keeps its history.

Decisions get explained where explaining them does not expose the person who
reported. Repeat behaviour, or anything aimed at a person rather than the work,
goes straight to a block.
